implementation: Typed descriptor size and selected provider/pin in Staged::Content; absent legacy hash is never interpreted as an empty typed file. Legacy paths remain. Unintegrated native writable/snapshot/resize/direct staged read fail explicitly.

One-time optional Engine provider seam, lazy default local provider off-lock. Capture selection, pin and read outside Engine, revalidate view/handle/selection at completion. Pin identity checked; failed provisional opens released; concurrent losing pins released outside Engine. Lease release contract forbids disk/network I/O.

Provider calls <=1MiB. Public API short reads <=1MiB; WinFsp fills its borrowed destination through bounded calls without false EOF; FUSE allocates only after native selection within existing <=1MiB reply limit. Per-request context links object-worker stop, deadline bounds Engine polling. Arbitrary blocking provider/OS operations are not forcibly interrupted.

Clean nonwriter refresh updates complete Entry metadata plus selected bytes. Same descriptor preserves pin. Dirty/writer base preservation and unlinked-open behavior remain. Stale output discarded and transferred zero on WinFsp failure. FUSE open uses existing bounded threaded dispatcher.

Move legacy cancellation hooks outside inflight-objects mutex, preserving content-state snapshot order after cancel. Six old Unix Clippy 1.96 diagnostics corrected without suppressions: two nested ifs, four signal function-pointer casts.
qualification: Ten new regular parents cover known size and pin lifetime with a truly missing unrelated chunk; missing root/corrupt demanded bytes; empty/EOF and native guards; >2MiB Win ABI read versus bounded provider/FUSE calls; blocked pin and bad pin with independent metadata; blocked I/O and concurrent real revision refresh refusing stale bytes; same-reference refresh preserving pin and full timestamps/revision; legacy zero-wait and stale generation; Engine-lock deadline; mid-read cancellation and lifetime. The explicit opt-in mounts real fixture stores through WinFsp/FUSE, reads a partial available file and >2MiB complete file, refuses missing-demand/write-open, refreshes bytes/length/timestamp of the same OS handle, releases pins and detaches cleanly. Other selected suites are regressions for the affected runtime/provider/journal/publication contracts.
development: Preliminary Windows release and Linux development runs passed eight new parents and separate real kernel mounts before two extra parents/stop-order review. Initial Rust type errors corrected; intermediate fmt output corrected. Linux default Rust1.88 strict lint stopped at an old uninlined-format test warning; installed named minimal1.96 with Clippy (default unchanged) to align compilers. Linux1.96 exposed six old Unix-only diagnostics, corrected before refreeze. A Linux regression attempt then reported content_transport41/42: the legacy foreground test had already passed admission/availability/byte assertions, but sampled the final frame completion counter before its asynchronous update (admitted5/started5/completed4/running1). The test now waits for that acknowledgement separately before cancelling, with the same one-second bound and unchanged admission/byte timing; no timing gate was relaxed. Sources refrozen and both full selections rerun. Windows qualifications already live during source corrections are unbound preliminary outputs. No draft count is final qualification.
compatibility: No schema/canonical/wire/event changes, private user_version4. Existing WinFsp DisableCache and FUSE direct-I/O settings unchanged. Only private temporary fixture stores were mounted; no live user migration, capability activation or native CAS deletion.
additional_development_diagnostics: The first acknowledgement-wait expression triggered nonminimal_bool in strict Clippy on both platforms; simplified to Option::is_none_or before the final freeze. Both failed lint logs and their source snapshot are retained.

One Windows build attempted to relink content_transport while an earlier unbound test process still executed that same cached binary; LINK LNK1104/exit101. Its log is retained. The earlier process was allowed to finish before rebuilding. No source workaround, shortened test or extra success count.

The unbound Windows suite subsequently reported pending_saves8/9: the retained-save writer probe saw only18 samples (17 free,1 held), below its unchanged minimum20, as the 32MiB save completed quickly. Armed the existing engine.save.store hook for400ms/count1 in this test, with RAII reset and asserted hit, so it samples slow byte work deterministically. Kept the minimum20 and free ratio>=0.3; writer-before-store still fails this regression. New final snapshot followed. Linux attempts already live during test corrections are unbound and separately retained before final rerun.
not_qualified: Foreground missing-range demand/lease scheduling and availability-index repair are not wired to these callbacks. This proves ready local ranges with unrelated missing chunks; not remote demand latency/fairness/outage behavior.

Native COW mounted writes, durable namespace/create/delete/rename/atomic replacement/open-handle identity recovery, complete close/fsync fences, startup enumeration/autonomous retry and Engine quiet/checkout/shutdown/status integration remain required.

Automatic close-producer coalescing, compatible metadata batching, independent private readers under slow FULL fsync, complete root registry/deletion barriers/actual native GC races, live retained fallback and receipt-owned retirement/storage progress remain incomplete.

All residual WP6.3/6.5/6.6 work and original two-peer/ENOSPC/power-loss/OS-close/allocation/matched builds/load/outage/30-minute soak/physical amplification/actual old-executable migration/downgrade/capability/handoff gates remain open. Real isolated read mounts do not qualify mounted build speed or native save durability. No gate is waived.
